text:
Maya: quick heads-up, planning to merge quant-kernel v3.2.2 into main tonight. Need a tight premerge + canary runbook and a deterministic fallback for dedicated pools. Tagging @Dan @Zhao @Tiffany @Juan and ops.

Dan: checklist? smoke matmul latency, kv-cache parity, regressions by model. Define rollback thresholds.

Zhao: telemetry: 1m QPS-weighted matmul p95, median token latency, kv-cache miss-rate. Rollback if matmul p95 > +14% for 5m or kv-miss > 1.5% for 4m.

Maya: rollout plan: 0.25% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30%, 8-15m watch windows. Start regional throttles to avoid hotspots.

Tiffany: Ill draft RN with validated model matrix and note on int8 packing. Will post link pre-merge.

Juan: recommend we pin dedicated-prod to v3.1.9 pre-deploy and automate a routing flip back if rollback triggered. Ops, can you prepare automation?

OpsBot: deploy window 23:45-01:00 UTC. Canary automation supports staged slices and auto-revert on alerts. Routing toggle script available.

Dan: add a preflight: deploy-bot preflight quant-smoke in staging, expect <=2% perf delta and zero kv errors.

BuildBot: CI 3.2.2-rc built; perf median -0.6% vs baseline. Artifacts at gs://redwood-builds/quant-kernel/3.2.2-rc.

Maya: owners: Dan first-responder, Zhao telemetry, Juan routing, Tiffany comms. I will merge after RN link + preflight PASS.

BuildBot: preflight PASS (matmul p95 +0.9%, kv-miss 0.0%). Promoting artifact.

OpsBot: rolling out: stage1 0.25% observing. Reply +1 to confirm.

Maya: +1. monitoring stage1.

BuildBot: stage1 stable -> advancing. stage2 2% live. matmul p95 +1.4%, kv-miss 0.2%.

Zhao: watching p95 slope; alert rule set at +12% for 5m.

OpsBot: stage3 10% live. No auto rollback.

Maya: leaving dedicated pin for 90m post-deploy. If any sustained signal, Juan flip routing and notify.

Tiffany: RN posted: internal link. Announce queued.

Dan: standing by for 2h clear then close thread. If any noisy regressions, we flip and open incident.

Maya: initial rollout complete, no rollback. Will file post-deploy note and follow up on model-level evals. :tada:
